title: Always On Top transparency doesn't work properly with Crop & Lock
summary: The screenshots describe effects targeting the source instead of the visible Crop and Lock host. Reparent and thumbnail modes have different HWND ownership, so confirm the mode before changing Always On Top target resolution.

next_action.label: Review issue-specific next step
next_action.reason: Thanks for the comparison screenshots and the Link to Windows app details. Which Crop and Lock mode was used: Thumbnail (Win+Ctrl+Shift+T) or Reparent (Win+Ctrl+Shift+R)? Does the same sequence affect a simple Notepad window, and does switching the crop mode change the result? Please also confirm the exact PowerToys version shown in Settings. This identifies whether the source-child versus visible-host window is being selected, rather than assuming all crop modes share the same target.

proposed_fixes.title: Capture source, foreground and crop-host HWND relationships separately for reparent and thumbnail modes.
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: the foreground/child HWND selected in reparent mode differs from the top-level crop host, leaving border/alpha on the wrong surface.
plan: Capture source, foreground and crop-host HWND relationships separately for reparent and thumbnail modes.
If wrong-target selection is confirmed, resolve the intended crop host at the module boundary without applying a global GetAncestor rule to unrelated apps.
Restore prior alpha/styles and pin state when the crop closes.
verification: Border and transparency affect the visible crop host in the supported mode.
Uncropping restores the source; ordinary pinned windows and thumbnail crops do not regress.
